No, oblique views do not add significant value in the diagnosis of spondylolysis in adolescents. While they are considered standard practice by some, our data indicates that there is no diagnostic benefit that outweighs the additional cost and radiation exposure.

In fact, four-view studies have shown similar sensitivity and specificity to two-view studies for detecting spondylolysis, suggesting that oblique views may not provide any significant advantages in this specific diagnosis.
